entry: Intercepted letter to Charles I, 13 May 1646
text_and_source: BL Add MS 72438 f.10 (DECODE R8624, login); transcription by Aymeloglu (royalist-1646/f10_ct.txt, 735 tokens)
size: 735 tokens, about 173 distinct word codes, max 697
system_known: Aymeloglu (16 Sept 2026): same cipher as the King's letters to Nicholas of 24 June and 16 Aug 1646 (Evelyn iv.178-179); about 45 values; he names it "Digby key no. 129"
teams_tried_and_where_they_stopped: Aymeloglu: annealing fails, "needs the decipher or the rest of the key"; cipher-lab (2-4 Oct): key confirmed against page images, 164-192 of 735 tokens keyed, judge FAIL, "not reading ready"
our_first_view: LARGEST TEXT. New link (ours): the word list is the King's Titus cipher of 1648 (Hillier 1852 prints 15 letters with decipherment) with a shift of +4 (a-h), 0 (i-n), +1 (o-t), +8/+9 (w-y and all above). 647 43 20 280 681 = "fif-t-h of May"; the King's reply of 2 June names "one letter from you, which was of the 5th of May". Writer: Nicholas at Oxford.
